title: Design Caching Strategy for High-Traffic Application
question: Design a comprehensive caching strategy for a high-traffic e-commerce application handling 10K requests/second. Requirements: 1) Cache product catalog (100K products, updated hourly), 2) Cache user sessions (1M active users), 3) Cache shopping cart (short-lived, frequently updated), 4) Cache search results (personalized, varies by user), 5) Handle cache invalidation when products updated, 6) Minimize database load while ensuring data freshness, 7) Support geographic distribution (multi-region caching). Discuss: using Redis cluster for distributed caching with consistent hashing, implementing multi-level caching (L1: local Caffeine cache for hot data like top products, L2: Redis for distributed access), caching product catalog with 1-hour TTL and cache-aside pattern, using Redis hash for product details (HGETALL product:123), storing user sessions in Redis with session ID as key and 30-minute sliding expiration, implementing shopping cart with write-through cache (update DB + Redis simultaneously) using Redis hash for cart items, caching search results with composite key (query+user_id+filters) and shorter TTL (5 minutes) due to personalization, implementing cache warming at startup for top 1000 products, using pub/sub for cache invalidation (when product updated, publish ProductUpdated event, all app instances evict cache), implementing cache-aside with double-check locking for cache stampede prevention, using Redis replication across regions with eventual consistency, monitoring cache hit ratio per cache type, and implementing circuit breaker for cache failures (fallback to database).

title: Maintain Cache-Database Consistency
question: Design system to maintain consistency between cache and database. Requirements: 1) Updates to database must be reflected in cache, 2) Handle concurrent updates to same data, 3) Prevent stale reads from cache, 4) Support cache invalidation patterns, 5) Handle cache failures gracefully, 6) Implement cache warming strategies. Discuss: using write-through pattern (update DB then cache atomically), implementing versioning with optimistic locking (version column in DB, increment on update, invalidate cache if version mismatch), using cache-aside with TTL as eventual consistency mechanism, implementing event-driven invalidation (after DB update, publish event to invalidate cache), using CDC (Change Data Capture with Debezium) to capture DB changes and invalidate cache automatically, handling race conditions with Redis WATCH/MULTI/EXEC for atomic read-check-set, implementing distributed locks (Redisson) for critical sections, using cache stamped (store timestamp with cached data, compare with DB timestamp), implementing read-through cache that checks DB if cache stale, warming cache on application startup or scheduled job, handling cache miss storms with single-flight pattern (only first request loads from DB, others wait), and monitoring staleness metrics.

title: Implement Distributed Session Management
question: Design distributed session management for clustered application. Requirements: 1) Share sessions across multiple application instances, 2) Handle server failures without losing sessions, 3) Support session expiration and renewal, 4) Scale to millions of concurrent sessions, 5) Maintain session affinity when needed, 6) Minimize latency for session access. Discuss: using Spring Session with Redis as session store, storing session data in Redis hash with session ID as key, configuring sticky sessions at load balancer for performance (same user routes to same server, but session still in Redis for failover), implementing sliding session expiration (update Redis TTL on each request), using Redis Sentinel or Cluster for high availability, storing minimal data in session (only user ID, fetch rest from database/cache as needed), implementing session replication across data centers for geographic distribution, using JSON serialization for cross-language compatibility, handling session fixation with session ID regeneration after login, implementing concurrent session limits per user (store active session IDs in Redis set), cleaning up expired sessions with background job, and monitoring session count and memory usage.

title: Implement Rate Limiting with Redis
question: Design API rate limiting using Redis. Requirements: 1) Limit requests per user (100 req/minute), 2) Different limits for different user tiers (free, premium), 3) Distributed rate limiting across servers, 4) Return clear error with retry-after when limit exceeded, 5) Support both user-based and IP-based limiting, 6) Efficient algorithm handling high throughput. Discuss: implementing token bucket algorithm with Redis, using Redis key rate_limit:user:123 with value as token count, using INCR for atomic increment and checking against limit, implementing sliding window with Redis sorted set (ZADD with timestamp score, ZCOUNT to check rate in time window, ZREMRANGEBYSCORE to cleanup old entries), using Redis Lua script for atomic rate limit check and increment, storing rate limit config in Redis hash (user_tier:limits), returning 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After header, implementing IP-based rate limiting for anonymous users, using Redis pipelining for performance, handling burst allowance (allow temporary spike above limit), resetting counters with TTL (EXPIRE command), distributing load with Redis Cluster, and monitoring rate limit hits per user tier.

title: Design Real-Time Leaderboard with Redis
question: Implement real-time leaderboard for gaming application. Requirements: 1) Track scores for millions of players, 2) Update scores in real-time, 3) Query top 100 players globally, 4) Get player rank and surrounding players, 5) Support multiple leaderboards (daily, weekly, all-time), 6) Handle high write throughput (10K updates/second). Discuss: using Redis sorted set (ZSET) for leaderboard storage, player ID as member and score as score value, using ZADD to update player score (O(log N) complexity), using ZREVRANGE to get top N players, using ZREVRANK to get player's rank, using ZREVRANGE with player rank ±10 to get surrounding players, implementing multiple leaderboards with different keys (leaderboard:daily:2024-03-28, leaderboard:weekly:2024-W13, leaderboard:alltime), using scheduled job to reset daily/weekly leaderboards, implementing score ties with timestamp as tiebreaker (score + microseconds), using Redis pipelining for batch updates, sharding leaderboards by region for scalability, caching leaderboard results with short TTL (10 seconds) to reduce Redis load, implementing incremental score updates (ZINCRBY), and monitoring leaderboard size and update latency.

title: Identify and Fix Performance Bottlenecks
question: Diagnose and resolve performance bottlenecks in slow application. Requirements: 1) Application response time increased from 100ms to 2s, 2) Database CPU at 90%, 3) Memory usage growing steadily, 4) Frequent garbage collection pauses, 5) Some API endpoints much slower than others, 6) Performance degrades during peak traffic. Discuss: using APM tools (New Relic, Datadog) to identify slow transactions, analyzing database with slow query log to find unoptimized queries, using EXPLAIN ANALYZE to understand query execution plan, adding indexes on frequently filtered columns, identifying N+1 queries with Hibernate statistics, implementing eager fetching with JOIN FETCH for required associations, analyzing heap dump with Eclipse MAT to find memory leaks, identifying objects retained in memory (check for static collections, unclosed resources), tuning JVM with appropriate heap size based on profiling, enabling G1GC for better pause times, analyzing GC logs to optimize garbage collection, identifying slow endpoints with distributed tracing, implementing caching for frequently accessed data, using Redis for session storage instead of in-memory, optimizing expensive computations with caching, implementing connection pooling with HikariCP and tuning pool size, using async processing for long-running operations, implementing rate limiting to protect against traffic spikes, and load testing to verify improvements.
